svg.title: URL Security Platform: Algorithm-First Filter Pipeline Architecture
svg.desc: Two-stage architecture: classical algorithm filters (bloom filter variants, trie, heuristics) pre-screen URLs before the ML core receives only high-risk candidates

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What URL formats should the input layer handle?')
sendPrompt('Explain Counting Bloom Filter vs Standard Bloom Filter for URL security')
sendPrompt('How does a Scalable Bloom Filter work and why is it better for dynamic URL lists?')
sendPrompt('What is a Cuckoo Filter and how does it improve on bloom filters for URL screening?')
sendPrompt('How should I implement an ensemble voting mechanism across multiple bloom filter variants?')
sendPrompt('How do I build a compressed Trie (radix tree) for fast domain prefix matching of malicious domains?')
sendPrompt('What heuristic rules should I apply on URL structure before sending to ML? Entropy, special chars, URL length?')
sendPrompt('What threshold logic should decide if a URL is passed to the ML core vs returned as Safe immediately?')
sendPrompt('What data should we return for a URL that is cleared by Stage 1 filters without reaching ML?')
sendPrompt('What happens to suspicious borderline URLs at Stage 1 — do they go to ML or get flagged differently?')
sendPrompt('How should the URL expansion module work with redirects in the ML pipeline?')
sendPrompt('What features should the feature extractor produce from a URL for the ML model?')
sendPrompt('What ML model architecture works best for malicious URL classification?')
sendPrompt('What should the final API response schema look like including Stage 1 filter metadata?')
sendPrompt('What does the React dashboard need to display for Stage 1 filter decisions vs Stage 2 ML results?')

svg.text: Click any node for implementation guidance ↗
